thesis: {ready} of 100 apps can become an agent toolkit today, {friction} more with friction, {blocked} are blocked. The gate is almost never technical: it is who hands out credentials. Self-serve developer access is the norm ({selfserve}/100); the hard cases cluster in ads, commerce, finance and enterprise-sold tools, where app review or a sales contract stands between Composio and a test key ({human_gate} of {nonready} non-ready apps).

findings.title: OAuth2 dominates, but rarely alone
findings.body: {oauth} apps offer OAuth2 and {static} offer a static credential (API key, bearer/PAT or Basic). {both} offer both, so a toolkit can ship an API-key path for single-tenant users and OAuth for multi-tenant installs. Only {oauth_only} are OAuth-only.

findings.title: Self-serve is the default; gating clusters by segment
findings.body: Dev infra and productivity tools are near-universally free to build on ({devprod_free}/20 free tier or sandbox). Gates concentrate in Marketing & ads (Google/Meta/LinkedIn app review), E-commerce (paid stores, seller registration) and Finance (production approval, customer-only accounts). Two quieter patterns: support desks are trial-only ({support_trial}/10: credentials expire with the trial), and AI tools charge first ({ai_paid}/10 need a paid plan).

findings.title: Official MCP is now table stakes
findings.body: {mcp_official} vendors already publish an official MCP server (many launched in 2025-26; several are docs-search-only or beta). Existence of an MCP is no longer the differentiator. Managed auth, multi-tenant credentials, and consistent tool quality across apps are.

findings.title: Most blockers are a person, not a missing API
findings.body: Of the {nonready} apps that are not ready today, {human_gate} wait on a human gate (app review, developer-token approval, partner program or a sales contract). {paid_gate} need a paid plan and only {no_api} lack a hosted API. This is an outreach problem more than an engineering one: start partner conversations in parallel with building.

ver_lede: Pass 1 was checked three ways: a deterministic link-and-claim checker over all {urls1} evidence URLs, independent adversarial verifier agents told to refute every flagged record, and a blind sample of 20 apps labelled from vendor pages in a real browser before any agent output was read. Accuracy on the sample went from {acc1_raw}% (pass 1 vs the original labels) to {acc2}% after the loops; {perfect2}/20 apps are now right on every field.
acc_note: Grey = pass 1, green = final. Sample: random.Random(2026), 2 apps per block of 10, labelled before any agent output was read. Scored fields: auth (set match), access tier, MCP status, buildability verdict. Pass 1 against the corrected labels was {acc1}%. Remaining miss: Clay buildability. Verifiers found its free API is narrow (~15 endpoints, 100 results / 30 days), which the prompt's own rules class as friction; the gold said ready. Left as a miss rather than re-labelled.
funnel: apps flagged: claim not on cited page, low confidence, or agent asked for help
evidence / notes upgrades (weak citation replaced by a vendor page)
apps re-checked in a real browser where agents got 403 / JS-only pages (loop 3; {changes_browser} further changes)
apps still marked for human review

pipeline.d: Scraped from the brief's virtualized Notion table in a real browser (a plain fetch returned an empty shell).
prompt.md fixes the vocabulary (6 access tiers, 3 verdicts) so 100 answers are comparable and machine-checkable.
5 parallel agents × 20 apps, web search + fetch, vendor docs first, JSON per app with evidence URLs and confidence. Headless version: agent/research.py.
Fetches every evidence URL, checks it resolves and that the page actually mentions the claimed auth method / MCP. No LLM.
A stronger model re-researches only flagged records with the instruction to refute, and must cite a vendor URL for every change.
Pages agents could not load (403 / JS-rendered: Salesforce, Otter, Lark docs) were opened in a real browser. Rows still ambiguous keep a 'human' badge for a person to sign off.
20 seeded-random apps labelled from vendor pages in a browser before any agent output was read; disagreements re-adjudicated against vendor pages, all changes logged.
score.py reports per-field accuracy; build.py merges loops, buckets blockers, renders this page, JSON and CSV.

run.lede: Everything after pass 1 runs offline with no API key. The research stage runs headless against an LLM API (Anthropic SDK); the verify, score and build stages are plain Python. 21 offline tests cover the schema, scorer, link flags and the research runner (malformed JSON repair, pause-turn resume, fail-closed fallback, cache reuse).
run.cmds:
pip install -r requirements.txt

# pass 1: headless research agent (needs ANTHROPIC_API_KEY or `ant auth login`)
python -m agent.research data/apps.json data/pass1/results.json --limit 5   # smoke test

# loop 1: deterministic evidence + claim checker (no key)
python -m agent.verify_links data/pass1/results.json data/pass1/link_report.json

# accuracy on the blind sample
python -m agent.score data/pass1/results.json data/final/results.json

# merge loops, compute patterns, render site/index.html + results.json/csv
python -m agent.build

python -m pytest -q tests
run.limits: Honest limits: in this submission, pass 1 and loop 2 were run as interactive AI research agents (Anthropic models, operated by the author) using the same prompt and schema as research.py; the headless script is unit-tested against a fake client but was not run against the live API (no API key in the build environment). Gold labels were taken from vendor pages in a real browser; the human_confirmed flag on each row of data/gold.json records the author's own re-check. 20 apps × 4 fields is a small sample, so treat ±5 pts as noise. Access tiers change often (several free plans were retired in 2025-26); every row carries its evidence URL so it can be re-checked.
